=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (lines 10542-10557 in last_run_diff, matching hunk in PR diff)
  Line or code reference: `_std_cached_head_sha` extraction + `jq -cn` cache-seeding block (and its mirror at ~10794)
  Problem: The GraphQL-sourced `head.sha` is now seeded into `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED`, but the downstream `# Widen the REST-fallback trigger` comment and later re-fetch logic still treat a completely blank `head_branch` as the sole signal for "in-flight review run". When the `pulls/{n}` re-fetch is forced to fail (as covered by the new test), the blank-head guard can still race an empty-commit push against an already-queued `workflow_dispatch` review run.
  Why it fails at runtime: The test `test_standalone_retrigger_review_uses_graphql_head_sha_when_pulls_refetch_fails` asserts zero pushes, but the cached JSON construction only adds `sha` when the extracted value is non-empty; transient GraphQL nulls or whitespace can still drop the SHA, letting the race re-occur under load.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh (lines 1407-1414 and 1682-1699)
  Line or code reference: `_tmp_output_first_nonempty_line` capture + `printf '%s\n' "${_tmp_output_first_nonempty_line}" | grep -qiE` (both the structured-validation block and the retry short-circuit)
  Problem: The first-non-empty-line scoping is present, but `grep -m1 -vE '^[[:space:]]*$'` can produce an empty string on a completely blank `tmp_output` (or when the file is truncated mid-write by the watchdog). The downstream `if printf ... | grep` then silently succeeds (no refusal match), so a true refusal that happens to be on line 2+ can be misclassified as a valid structured summary.
  Why it fails at runtime: The editor refusal short-circuit and the later `EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL` validator both rely on this capture; a partially-written or whitespace-only output would bypass the sentinel, letting the refusal fallback marker be omitted and the orchestrator poller treat the run as "suspicious noop" instead of "model refused — re-run after cache expiry". The new test only exercises a full refusal example, not the empty-output edge.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: agents.md (new row at ~263)
  Line or code reference: `| `PR_PROCESSED_ALERT_LEVEL` | `SILENT` | …`
  Problem: The variable was added to the review-pipeline table in this PR, but the canonical doc location for alert-level knobs (including the `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` defaulting logic and the `update_workflows.yml` exception) is `probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md` §20.4 and the top-level variables table in README.md. Duplicating the row without updating the runbook cross-reference creates a documentation drift that future refactors will miss.
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime breakage, but the contract-test `test_noop_warning_literal_present_in_poller()` style of lockstep checking cannot catch it; operators will see inconsistent docs when they grep for alert-level knobs.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2 (pure documentation, low operational risk)
- Requirement: "Resolve the conflicts and merge this PR so the bug fix on `stable` is also present on `main`." (from the PR description) plus the explicit list of conflicting files including `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `mark-stable.yml`, `review_autofix.yml`, `test-and-mark-stable.yml`, `README.md`, `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`, `orchestrate_*`, `review_*`, and multiple test files.

  Evidence of absence: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` (and the last_run_diff_stat) shows only the nine documentation/test-orchestrator files; the workflow and script files listed in the PR description still carry the stable-side changes that were never re-applied on main after the initial merge-resolve.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
